name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+17, among the most Democratic seats in Maryland
Boafo holds a decisive money edge: $1.9M raised and $12.1M in outside support versus no visible Republican fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
Open seat after Hoyer's retirement adds modest uncertainty with no polling available
model.rationale: The district's D+17 lean, Boafo's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and market pricing near 97% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat; nothing in the record suggests Republican competitiveness.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharply favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Maryland's 5th District leans 17 points Democratic, and Steny Hoyer's retirement hands the seat to a well-funded successor rather than putting it in play. Democrat Adrian Boafo has raised about $1.9 million and drawn roughly $12.1 million in outside support, while Republican Chris Chaffee shows no reported fundraising or outside spending. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. The open-seat nature of the contest adds a modest layer of uncertainty, but a district this Democratic has rarely been competitive in a general election. The expected margin sits in the low twenties for Boafo, consistent with recent Democratic performance in the Washington suburbs and with the seat's long partisan history.
